pharm: Selective postjunctional alpha-1 adrenoceptor blocker that relaxes vascular and prostatic/bladder-neck smooth muscle, lowering blood pressure and easing bladder outlet obstruction.
quick: Start 1 mg once daily; titrate to max 8 mg (BPH) or 16 mg (HTN)
May take with or without food (food effect not clinically significant)
Limited data; untreated hypertension also carries maternal risk
Use with caution; monitor for hypotension
Blood pressure (esp. first dose and after titration); BPH: rule out prostate cancer
summary: Doxazosin is a selective alpha-1 adrenergic antagonist used to treat the signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and to lower blood pressure in hypertension. Therapy starts at 1 mg once daily and is titrated upward, with a maximum of 8 mg/day for BPH and 16 mg/day for hypertension. First-dose orthostatic hypotension and syncope can occur, so blood pressure should be monitored after the initial dose and each dose increase. Patients on alpha-1 blockers can develop Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome during cataract surgery.
indications: Treatment of the signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)
Treatment of hypertension to lower blood pressure and reduce cardiovascular risk

dosage.d: Start 1 mg once daily; titrate to 2 mg, then 4 mg and 8 mg
dosage.n: Titrate at 1 to 2 week intervals; maximum 8 mg once daily; routinely monitor blood pressure

dosage.d: Start 1 mg once daily; may double dose as needed

dosage.n: Monitor blood pressure for at least 6 hours after administration
If stopped for several days, restart using the initial dosing regimen

admin: Take once daily, in the morning or evening
May be taken with or without food
Monitor blood pressure for at least 6 hours after the first dose and after each dose increase
Titrate slowly (1 to 2 week intervals for BPH) to limit hypotension
If therapy is interrupted for several days, restart at the 1 mg initial dose
moa: Selectively and competitively blocks postjunctional alpha-1 adrenoceptors. In blood vessels this lowers systemic vascular resistance and blood pressure; in the prostatic stroma, capsule, and bladder neck it reduces smooth muscle tone, decreasing urethral resistance and relieving BPH outflow symptoms.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to doxazosin, other quinazolines (e.g., prazosin, terazosin), or any component
monitor: Blood pressure after first dose and each titration
Prostate cancer screening before and during BPH therapy

preg: Limited human data are insufficient to inform drug-associated risk for major birth defects or miscarriage; untreated hypertension in pregnancy itself increases maternal and fetal risk. Animal studies showed no adverse developmental effects at therapeutic-range exposures, with reduced fetal survival only at very high doses.
lact: Data on presence in human milk are limited; use with caution in breastfeeding women, weighing benefit against potential infant exposure.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is described in the label; doxazosin is highly protein bound and not dialyzable.
hepatic: Extensively metabolized by the liver; use with caution in hepatic impairment and monitor for hypotension.

major: PDE-5 inhibitors (e.g., sildenafil, tadalafil) - additive blood-pressure lowering and symptomatic hypotension
moderate: Strong CYP3A inhibitors - increased doxazosin exposure and hypotension risk; monitor blood pressure
interactions.food: Food slightly reduces Cmax (~18%) and AUC (~12%); not clinically significant - may take with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: Rule out prostate carcinoma before starting BPH therapy and at regular intervals afterward, since prostate cancer can mimic BPH symptoms.

serious: Postural (orthostatic) hypotension with or without syncope
Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome during cataract surgery
emergency: Syncope, especially after the first dose or a dose increase
Priapism (sustained painful erection requiring urgent care)

monitoring: Blood pressure for at least 6 hours after the first dose and after each titration
Routine blood pressure in BPH patients
Prostate cancer screening before and at intervals during BPH treatment
Symptoms of orthostatic hypotension and syncope
counsel: You may feel dizzy or faint, especially after the first dose, a dose increase, or restarting therapy
Avoid driving or hazardous tasks for 24 hours after the first dose, a dose increase, or restarting treatment
Rise slowly from sitting or lying down to reduce dizziness
Tell your eye surgeon you take this medicine before any cataract surgery
Seek immediate care for a prolonged or painful erection (priapism)
Report fainting or persistent dizziness to your healthcare provider
Be cautious combining with erectile dysfunction (PDE-5) drugs - blood pressure can drop
pk: Blood-pressure effect within hours; postural effects may appear within a few hours of dosing
Plasma peak about 2 to 3 hours after oral dosing
Store at 20 C to 25 C (68 F to 77 F); dispense in a tight, light-resistant container
pearls: First-dose phenomenon: orthostatic hypotension and syncope are most likely after the initial dose, a dose increase, or restarting - start at 1 mg and titrate slowly
Associated with Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome; stopping the alpha-blocker before cataract surgery does not appear to help - inform the surgeon instead
Always exclude prostate cancer before treating BPH, since it can cause similar symptoms
Bioavailability ~65% from first-pass hepatic metabolism; ~98% protein bound, so not removed by dialysis
Restart at the 1 mg initial dose if therapy has been interrupted for several days
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered the same day; if it is close to the next dose, skip it and resume once daily. Do not double up. If doses have been missed for several days, restart at 1 mg once daily and re-titrate.
overdose: The most likely effect is hypotension; treat with the patient supine and intravenous fluid expansion. Because doxazosin is highly protein bound, dialysis is not helpful. Provide supportive care.
